52091.author: Xinlong12580
52091.body:
## PR description

This PR adds an opt-in neural-network cluster parameter estimator, `PixelCPENNReco`, for Phase-1 barrel pixel hits. It is intended for R&D comparisons with the existing Generic and Template CPEs and does not change the default reconstruction workflow.

The CPE uses one combined ONNX model to predict the local x and y position offsets and uncertainties. Its inputs are the normalized one-dimensional cluster projections, total cluster charge, track incidence angles, and a model-category value selecting among the supported barrel geometries: Layer 1 flipped/unflipped, Layer 2, and the positive/negative module regions of Layers 3 and 4. The model outputs positions and uncertainties directly in centimetres. They are checked for finite, positive, and physically bounded values before they are used.

`PixelCPENNReco` derives from `PixelCPEGeneric` so that the standard Generic CPE can be used consistently whenever the NN is not applicable. Generic reconstruction is used for:

- FPIX hits, for which no NN model is provided;
- reconstruction without track angles;
- clusters that cannot be represented by the NN input dimensions; and
- non-finite, non-positive, or out-of-range NN outputs.

The implementation also handles Phase-1 big pixels using the topology API, orders wide rows and columns before expanding them, and uses the track prediction when converting the selected cluster centre into local coordinates so that detector surface deformations are taken into account.

The ONNX Runtime session is created and owned by `PixelCPENNRecoESProducer`. The producer obtains the same magnetic-field, Lorentz-angle, Lorentz-angle-width, and GenError conditions needed by `PixelCPEGeneric`, allowing the fallback to use the configuration and conditions of the standard Generic CPE.

No standard reconstruction configuration is changed. In user workflows, the new CPE is enabled by explicitly applying:

```python
from RecoLocalTracker.SiPixelRecHits.customizePixelCPENN import customizePixelCPENN
process = customizePixelCPENN(process)
```

An alternative model installed in the CMSSW search path can be selected with:

```python
process = customizePixelCPENN(process, "path/to/model.onnx")
```

The customizer copies the active `PixelCPEGenericESProducer` parameters, including era-dependent modifications, creates the NN ESProducer, and changes `TTRHBuilderAngleAndTemplate` and `TTRHBuilderAngleAndTemplateWithoutProbQ` to use `PixelCPENNReco`. Consequently, this customization affects the track-angle-dependent transient-hit/refit stage; it does not replace the CPE used by the initial `siPixelRecHits` production.

For automated integration testing, this PR adds the opt-in Run 3 2025 TTbar upgrade workflow `16834.187`. The workflow applies the same customizer only to the reconstruction step; it does not enable the NN CPE in existing workflows.

The ONNX Runtime dependency is attached only to the conventional `RecoLocalTrackerSiPixelRecHitsPlugins` library. It is not added to the main `RecoLocalTracker/SiPixelRecHits` library or to the Alpaka plugin library.

### Model file

The model is proposed for inclusion in the [`RecoLocalTracker-SiPixelRecHits` cms-data package](https://github.com/cms-data/RecoLocalTracker-SiPixelRecHits/pull/1), rather than in the CMSSW source repository. Once that data update and its cmsdist integration are available, it is resolved at job initialization through `edm::FileInPath`. The customizer defaults to:

```text
RecoLocalTracker/SiPixelRecHits/data/PixelCPENN/PixelCPENNReco_Run3_2025_v1.onnx
```

Workflows that do not apply the customization neither load the model nor instantiate the NN CPE.

### Scope and limitations

- NN inference is currently supported only for the four-layer Phase-1 barrel pixel detector.
- FPIX and no-track-angle reconstruction use `PixelCPEGeneric`.
- An invalid model path, incompatible tensor names, or an incompatible graph interface is treated as a configuration error and can terminate the job. Numerically invalid outputs from a compatible graph fall back to `PixelCPEGeneric`.
- The current implementation performs one combined x/y inference per applicable hit. Batching and performance optimization are outside the scope of this PR.
- The CPE is not enabled by a process modifier or by default. Outside the dedicated RelVal workflow, it must be activated explicitly with the customizer above.

Preliminary comparisons with the Generic and Template CPEs are available in this [Pixel Offline presentation](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1724615/contributions/7298449/attachments/3352468/6011613/Copy%20of%20Pixel-offline%209_29.pdf). These studies evaluated the NN CPE before the final ONNX/`FileInPath` packaging introduced here; the model and reconstruction method are the same, while the CMSSW integration interface has changed.

## PR validation

- The touched C++ sources were formatted with the CMSSW code-format target.
- `RecoLocalTracker/SiPixelRecHits` builds successfully in the target CMSSW release.
- `runTheMatrix.py -w upgrade -l 16834.187,17034.187 -j 4` completes successfully, with all five workflow steps passing.
- The topic changes `RecoLocalTracker/SiPixelRecHits` and adds the dedicated workflow variant in `Configuration/PyReleaseValidation`; it does not modify standard CFFs or commit model weights to the CMSSW source repository.
- `git diff --check` passes for the complete topic.
52091.title: [17.1.X]Adding a new opt-in neural-network cluster parameter estimator PixelCPENNReco

52328.author: mroguljic
52328.body:
backport of #52289 

Follow-up of #52060, which introduced the `SiPixelClusterShapeLimits` payload and `SiPixelClusterShapeLimitsRcd` in 17.0.X (and got included into 17.1.X).

`ClusterShapeHitFilterESProducer` now reads the pixel cluster shape limits from `SiPixelClusterShapeLimitsRcd` in GT by default, instead of the `.par` files. This makes it possible to update the CSF limits through the GT, without a new release. 

This backport keeps the parameters `PixelShapeFile` and `PixelShapeFileL1` following [this comment](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/52328#pullrequestreview-5720873946): they are used only with the new parameter `usePixelShapeLimitsFromDB = False` (default `True`), so the HLT menus stay valid without a customisation. `customizeRun3_2026PixelShapePayloads` now also sets `usePixelShapeLimitsFromDB = False`.

No changes in the output are expected: the payloads in the GTs were written from the same `.par` files that are used today.

The PR must be tested together with the autoCond update to the new GTs (https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/52327), since the current GTs do not contain the new record.

Backport of #52214.

I cherry-picked the commit to the `custom_nano_cff.py` file and implemented in the latest image available `CMSSW_17_0_X_2026-10-29-2300`. The idea is for this to appear in 17_1_X.

##### Description from the original PR.
Adds two jet b-tagging discriminators of the jet matched to each muon to the custom muon NanoAOD (PhysicsTools/NanoAOD/python/custom_muon_cff.py):

Muon_jetPNetB: ParticleNet b vs. udscg score
Muon_jetUParTB: UParT b vs. udscg score
They follow the same pattern as the existing Muon_jetDF and Muon_jetCSVv2 variables. They use jetForLepJetVar, the same jet used as input to the prompt MVA, and default to -1 when there is no matched jet.

The idea is to integrate this into v16 nanoAODs.

52370.author: RobertJWard
52370.body:
Forward port of https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/52352
targeting 17_1_X.

#### PR description:

This PR updates the Phase-2 Global Trigger Emulator step-1 menu to use the latest online-to-offline scalings from [L1T annual review 2026](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1709561/), derived with the [standalone menu tools](https://github.com/cms-l1-dpg/Phase2-L1MenuTools) AR26 configs using CMSSW_17_0_0_pre6 (identical to pre7 in terms of L1 objects in the menu). 

It also adds three new menus as options for the P2GT step, e.g. `-s L1P2GT:v0p0_2026`, containing the seeds already available to be run in P2GT. The default stays `step1_2024`:
- `step1p5_2026`: the new core menu based on the Run 3 menu
- `v0p0_2026`: step 1.5 plus the available step 2 seeds and the extended-eta seeds, which will become the new baseline going forwards
- `step1and2_2026`: `step1_2024` plus the available step 2 seeds that weren't yet in the emulator, i.e the previous baseline

Seeds not-yet implementable in P2GT include the L1 Calo Tau seeds, the L1 Track-Triplet W->3pi seed, the b-tag L1 NG JetSC4 seed, and the two wide-jet L1 JetSC8 seeds that use the mass variable. The standalone L1EG seeds (both normal and extended) still use the stand-in of TkPhotons without applying isolation, but the two are equivalent physically and just differ in where the inputs come from (CL2 vs GCT).

In addition to the new menus, this updates the collection and format used in P2GT for the wide-jet objects (which hadn't previously been used in P2GT seeds) in line with the latest developments, and the thresholds in the triple TkMuon step 1 seed have been corrected (4/2 GeV to 3.5/2.5 GeV, to match the name and implementation in standalone tools). 

#### PR validation:  

In preparation: running the standard Phase-2 tests for the default `step1_2024` menu, and a comparison of standalone tools vs P2GT rates for each of the four menus: `step1_2024`, `step1and2_2026`, `step1p5_2026` and `v0p0_2026`

This is a backport PR targeting the 17_1_0 release.
52370.title: [17_1_X] [L1T] Update P2GT Emulator with Scalings from Annual Review 2026 and add additional menu options (Phase 2)

52381.body:
#### PR description:

Follow up PR to https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/52370 correcting an issue where the newer input collection used to produce SC8 jets (as of CMSSW_17_0_0_pre6) isn't yet available in event content, causing tests that run starting from L1P2GT without rerunning L1 to fail. This PR reverts to the older collection (used up to CMSSW_17_0_0_pre5) to fix this issue, where the performance between the two collections is comparable in P2GT.
